    How it works
    
  
    
  
    
    
    
      insert
      
    Both ways, really. Inserting from the toolbar splices a block into the
        source. Renaming, editing, indenting, connecting and deleting do too. The text stays the
        object, so your formatting survives.
    
    
    
    
    
      ## → ###
      
    Heading depth is containment. Indent moves ## to
        ### and the node slides inside the group above it. JSON Canvas cannot say
        this, which is why its Mermaid emitter flattens groups to plain boxes.
    
    
    
    
    
      drag
      
    Layout is presentation. Drag and the source stays put. Switch on
        Positions and @x,y appears, because now a human placed it
        deliberately. Which side port you grab never reaches the file either.
    
    
    
    
    
      tag=
      
    One structure, three renderings. A heading in the file, a group on the
        canvas, and nested <tags> for the agent. Tagging is inherited, so a
        tagged section wraps its children too.
    
    
    
    
    
      okf
      
    Frontmatter is OKF. Google's Open Knowledge Format. type is
        the only required field; extension keys are explicitly allowed, so inserting a schema
        merges rather than clobbers.
    
    
    
    
    
      keys
      
    Shortcuts. The pencil jumps to and selects the authored heading in the
        source pane; double-click edits a node directly on the canvas. Cmd+A, Delete,
        Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z, Cmd+C / X / V on the canvas. Drag on empty space to marquee-select.
        In the source pane the native ones apply.
    
    
    
    
    
      snap
      
    Clean by default. Dragging, resizing, and automatic layout use the
        20px grid and keep a two-cell gutter around the workflow. Auto removes pinned
        positions and fits the whole workflow. Collapse and expand discard stale manual sizing,
        measure the content again, and separate siblings that would otherwise overlap.
